Question ID: CW_U03_L07_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06

Scene plan: Central idea: maturity includes accepting guidance. Source influence: a guide gives an object before a journey. Character conflict: Maya thinks leaders work alone, while her teammate thinks leaders trust the group. Which choice best explains integration?

answer.text: A. The plan is integrated because every element supports shared responsibility.

feedback.text: Correct. The central idea, guide-object pattern, and perspective conflict all point to the same meaning.

answer.text: B. The plan is integrated because it has many unrelated parts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Integration requires connection, not just many parts.

answer.text: C. The source influence distracts because objects can never develop theme.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Objects can support theme when connected to conflict and growth.

answer.text: D. The conflict should be removed so the theme is easier.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Conflict helps develop the theme. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U03_L07_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.07

Passage: Jalen believed the mural had to be his design alone. When Amara handed him a sketch showing how everyone's ideas could fit, he erased his signature from the center and redrew the wall as a shared map. What changed understanding is shown?

answer.text: A. Jalen learns maps are never useful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The shared map becomes meaningful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Jalen decides art has no theme.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The mural develops theme. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Jalen avoids all collaboration.

feedback.text: Incorrect. He accepts Amara's input. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Jalen learns that leadership can include shared creative ownership.

feedback.text: Correct. He moves from control to collaboration. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U03_L07_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06

Scene goal: develop the idea that memory can guide a person forward. Which source influence best supports the goal?

answer.text: A. A random storm appears with no character effect.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The storm does not support the central idea by itself.

answer.text: B. A guide gives the character a family recipe before a move.

feedback.text: Correct. The guide-object pattern connects memory to future action.

answer.text: C. A character changes names only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Name changes do not build the idea.

answer.text: D. A scene lists furniture with no memory connection.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The details do not support the idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U03_L07_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.07

A student writes a fiction plan with a theme about honesty, a source influence about a magic doorway, and a character conflict about winning a race. None of the pieces affect each other. What is the best feedback?

answer.text: A. Keep it because unrelated pieces are always stronger.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unrelated pieces weaken focus. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Remove the theme from the plan.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Theme can guide integration. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Revise so the source influence, conflict, and theme all support one central idea.

feedback.text: Correct. Integrated fiction needs connected choices. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Add more unrelated objects.

feedback.text: Incorrect. More unrelated material increases the problem. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U03_L07_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06

Passage: Nia thought asking for help meant failure. Her grandmother gave her an old compass and said, "Even a compass needs a hand to hold it steady." Nia carried it to rehearsal and asked the director where to begin again. What source element and growth arc work together?

answer.text: A. Guide-object pattern and a shift from refusing help to accepting guidance.

feedback.text: Correct. The compass supports the character's changed understanding.

answer.text: B. A random object and no character change.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Nia's action changes by the end.

answer.text: C. A theme about cooking and a conflict about weather.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Neither appears. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A copied source with no transformation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The compass is adapted into a new realistic scene.
